summary: Blackwell Ultra is the mid-cycle refresh of NVIDIA's Blackwell generation: two reticle-sized TSMC 4NP dies (208 billion transistors) linked at 10 TB/s and presented to CUDA as a single GPU with up to 160 SMs, 640 fifth-generation Tensor Cores and 288 GB of HBM3E.

p: Each die carries four GPCs (eight in total) for up to 160 SMs. An SM pairs 128 CUDA cores with four fifth-generation Tensor Cores and 256 KB of dedicated tensor memory (TMEM) that holds accumulators close to the matrix units.

Relative to Blackwell, Ultra doubles the special-function-unit throughput for exponentials (about 10.7 tera-exponentials/s) to accelerate softmax in attention, and raises NVFP4 throughput via the second-generation Transformer Engine.

The L2 cache is shared and fully coherent across both dies; its capacity is not stated in the cited NVIDIA article. Off-package memory is HBM3E driven by sixteen 512-bit controllers (an 8,192-bit interface) for 8 TB/s. Capacity is configuration-dependent; 288 GB is the maximum.
As in other A1 designs, shared memory and TMEM give kernels explicit staging buffers, but the hierarchy as a whole is hardware-managed.

NVLink 5 provides 18 links at 100 GB/s (1.8 TB/s bidirectional per GPU) and can form a non-blocking domain of up to 576 GPUs; GB300 NVL72 racks use 72. NVLink-C2C connects to the Grace CPU at 900 GB/s, and the host interface is PCIe Gen 6 x16.
CUDA with dynamic warp scheduling; tensor work is expressed through CUTLASS/cuBLAS/cuDNN, Triton and TensorRT-LLM. An 800 GB/s decompression engine offloads data-loading work.
Warp-scheduled SIMT lanes with embedded tensor engines and a cache-centred hierarchy.

figures.title: Dual-die package (schematic)
figures.caption: Two dies joined by NV-HBI (10 TB/s). Each die shows four GPCs of 20 SMs — 160 SMs in total, matching the full implementation (shipping SKUs may enable fewer). Eight HBM3E stacks are shown; NVIDIA's article is internally inconsistent on the stack count.

figures.title: Blackwell Ultra SM
figures.caption: 128 CUDA cores and four fifth-generation Tensor Cores per SM, with 256 KB of tensor memory. L1/shared-memory capacity is not given in the cited article.

caveats: HBM capacity is configuration-dependent (e.g. 270–288 GB); 288 GB is not guaranteed for every module.
NVIDIA's article gives both 8 and 12 for the HBM3E stack count; the figure follows the 8 × 12-high (36 GB) arrangement.
